title: A substrate failure is never a verdict about the work
description:
Hold the line the Phase 1 reconciler already holds: a substrate failure is an
OPERATIONAL error and never a verdict about the work.

ticks gets this mostly right, and the good parts are the specification:
- collect/collect.go:108-109 — "an error means the check could not be performed
  ... never 'the worker failed', which is a verdict." Verdicts come only from
  git and the result file. Collect makes zero herdr calls.
- cleanup/cleanup.go:314-322 — a failed agent.list before a destructive step is
  a REFUSAL: "herdr did not answer is not evidence that tearing an agent down is
  safe." The re-check is taken next to the removal, not at run start.
- cleanup/cleanup.go:259-266 — blocked or working workers are never torn down.
- reconcile/reconcile.go:192-205 — an unreachable herdr aborts the whole report
  rather than classifying every tick dead. Unavailable, never wrong.
- wait/wait.go:106-128 — timeout and absent-worker are reported outcomes.
- notify/notify.go:423-428 — a transport refusal is deliberately not persisted,
  so it retries.
- spawn/spawn.go:218-220 — spawn never cleans up on failure; the failed pane
  stays as diagnostic state. No branch or workspace is deleted on a substrate
  error.

Where it does NOT hold, and which this tick must make impossible in ticfac:
- The gate-content failure (spawn.go:521-526) turns a rendering or truncation
  change into "the agent cannot work".
- Renaming agent_pane_busy or agent_prompt_stalled flips a tolerated condition
  into a hard failure (spawn.go:342-351, :404).

Do:
- Audit every herdr call site in the new executor and classify each failure
  explicitly: operational, or a verdict. Operational failures must not reject a
  tick, must not tear an attempt down, and must never delete a branch or a
  workspace.
- Map protocol and capability refusals to the operational side (the version tick
  raises them; this tick owns the tests).
- Resume across an upgrade: an attempt whose handle a later leg cannot address
  is HELD for a person, never redispatched.
- The test that settles it: a fixture where EVERY herdr call fails, asserting no
  tick is rejected, no attempt is torn down, and nothing is deleted.

acceptance_criteria: Every herdr call site in the executor classifies its failure as operational or verdict, and operational failures reject no tick, tear down no attempt and delete no branch or workspace; protocol and capability refusals are operational; an attempt whose handle a later leg cannot address is held for a person and never redispatched; a fixture in which every herdr call fails asserts no rejection, no teardown and no deletion; go test -short -timeout 45m ./... green.
